answer.evidence: The stairs are two olive treads (rows 0-4 and 8-11) that read as horizontal surfaces. Each tread ends in a lighter edge line followed by dark brown riser or shadow rows (rows 5-7 and 12-15), with a near-black outline at rows 7 and 15. Below the stairs, rows 16-31 are a flat olive cliff face about 16 rows tall. This matches a south-facing cliff with steps cut into it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts look better than the picture does. The candidate shows 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, and only 8% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown and count as dark_material_tone. But 50% of the candidate is near-flat, against 0% for both references. The lower half of the piece is one large tan/khaki fill with no grain, speckle or per-pixel variation. The upper part is a couple of dark brown horizontal bars with only 2-3 value steps. There are no individually shaded stones or peat texture, and nothing reads as steps rising through a cliff face. Next to the grass and cobble references, which are textured across the whole tile, it looks flatter and more sticker-like.
